Curated by hand: when a project is added, retired, renamed, or changes state/trigger, edit THIS file first, then run the generator. /new writes its entry here before scaffolding. The per-project CLAUDE.md baseline hashes are stored by `check.ps1 -Init` in state/baseline.json (NOT here); the claude_md_sha fields below are reserved/unused. The `hq_project` field is THE authoritative project->Alex-HQ metric-slug map (2026-07-07): work/16-alex-hq/scripts/build-projects.mjs reads it to render the HQ Automation Health board FROM this registry, so every registered project shows (not just the ones that push telemetry). null = the project pushes no live metric (its ticket shows an honest idle state).
meta.states_doc: LIVE = scheduled/event-driven + producing (needs wrapper/error-handler + HQ push). ON-DEMAND = runs when invoked. EVENT = triggered by a detected event, no cron by design. DORMANT = built, waiting on an external dependency (name it + revisit date; two unchanged revisits force activate-or-retire). PARKED = deliberately stopped (resume context + revisit date; same two-strike rule). RETIRED = superseded, tombstoned, strikethrough row. A project may carry LIVE or EVENT for at most 14 days with first_fire null (aging measured from its status.md frontmatter created date); past that the generator V9 warns and check.ps1 C13 goes amber until it fires (a documented drill counts, first_fire_kind=drill) or is re-stated with a reason.
meta.cadence_doc: Upgrade P4 (2026-07-12, design 1.3/MR2-3): `cadence` replaced the old per-day integer field. {expected_hours: N|null, label, note?} - expected_hours is the staleness window HQ/checks age against (null = never stale by age: on-demand/event/dormant/parked/retired); label drives the per-class render rules (design 4.2); note is the human phrase shown on monthly/odd cadences. Multi-job projects are keyed to the tightest job. `first_fire`/`first_fire_kind` (design 1.4/MR2-5): the date a project FIRST produced for real (null = never fired; kind live|drill - a documented drill counts as proof, marked honestly). RULING (2026-07-25, upgrade #18 P4 reconciling the 07-25 FR-02 downgrade): `expected_hours` is AUTHORITATIVE ONLY for HQ tile age-render (work/16-alex-hq/app/lib/types.ts cadenceStale ages the metric-push ts against it) - it is NOT the silence monitor. The authoritative outage detector is scripts/../work/16-alex-hq/scripts/n8n_liveness.py, which derives each workflow's window from its own scheduleTrigger, never this field. So a wrong expected_hours only mis-colors a tile, it can never miss a real outage. Field is KEPT (not deleted): it drives render and reads honestly; it is deliberately not load-bearing for detection, so it is never a cry-wolf source. `scope` (added 2026-07-25, stress-test F-06 follow-on): 'n8n-engine' means this cadence describes the project's REMOTE n8n workflow, not its local Windows job, so recovery C16 (a doc-vs-doc label compare against scheduler/schedule.md) SKIPS it and validator V6 leg (c) owns it instead by asserting `n8n_cron` against the live scheduleTrigger (doc-vs-reality, strictly stronger). Omitted/any other value = the cadence describes the local jobs and C16 checks it normally. #03 is why this exists: its engine runs Tue & Thu 15:00 on the box while PersonalOS-application-engine is a deliberately DAILY 08:30 local watch, so the two cadences are both correct and comparing them reports permanent false drift.
meta.n8n_cron_doc: Per-project SCHEDULE INTENT for a remote n8n workflow (added 2026-07-25, stress-test fix F-06). Optional; declare it on any project whose `n8n` workflow runs on a schedule. Validator V6 leg (c) asserts this string against the LIVE scheduleTrigger on every generator run and every commit, so an accidental or PUT-side-effect cron change FAILS instead of silently re-tuning the monitor. Root cause it kills: the HQ liveness monitor derives each workflow's silence window FROM the live trigger (self-referential, so a drifted cron looks healthy), and recovery C16 only compares two docs to each other. Format = a 5-field cron expression in the workflow's own timezone; n8n's interval-days trigger form is normalized to `<min> <hour> * * *` before comparison, and any other interval shape warns instead of failing. To retime a workflow deliberately: change the live trigger, then update this field in the same session (verify-after-write).

model_routing.doc: THE machine-authoritative model-routing contract (added 2026-07-24, born from the V6-blocked-generator bug: V6 used to derive its expectation by regex-parsing the CLAUDE.md prose rule, so the day the two engines got a documented Opus exception the prose gained a paragraph a regex could not read, and the checker false-failed and blocked the generator). Fix, general principle: a validator NEVER derives its expectation from prose - desired state lives here in structured data, and the check reads THIS. `default` = the model every n8n Claude node runs unless overridden. `overrides` = deliberate per-workflow exceptions (keyed by n8n workflow id). `checked_node` = the node whose model V6 asserts against the live n8n API. To change a model: edit here, then run the generator; validate-alex V6 enforces live-n8n == this contract (undocumented drift still fails; a documented change made here passes). Workflows in overrides that are NOT registered production engines (the eval harness) are warn-only, matching the prior semantics. NOTE (2026-07-27, kimi-k3 migration): the four job-lane overrides are now a NON-ANTHROPIC provider (Moonshot kimi-k3, OpenAI-compatible API), so `kimi`/`moonshot` were added to validate-alex's LLM_ID_RE model-id recognizer (without it V6 could not SEE the model string). The nodes call api.moonshot.ai/v1/chat/completions via the httpHeaderAuth credential 'Kimi K3 (Moonshot header)' (OffvMkWR01zcpqxo), not the anthropicApi credential; request bodies are OpenAI-format with reasoning_effort:'high' (rolled out at 'max' on 2026-07-27 morning, flipped to 'high' the same day after a measured comparison, see the override reasons). `default` stays claude-sonnet-4-6 for every other Claude node (e.g. #25 landscape-eval).

local_wrappers.doc: LOCAL model-pin contract for the scheduled `claude -p` wrappers under scripts/ (added 2026-07-25, stress-test fix F4). The n8n side is V6; this is its local twin, enforced by validate-alex V13. Root fix for the 'a wrapper forgets --model and inherits the global opus default' cost-leak class (the 2026-07-16 cut was convention-only until now). `pins` = every wrapper that makes a real `claude -p` reasoning call -> the exact --model it MUST pass. `deterministic_no_pin` = wrappers that make NO claude call (zero-token). V13 is COMPLETE by construction: every scripts/run-*.ps1 (+ auth-check.ps1) that calls `claude -p` MUST appear in pins or deterministic_no_pin, else V13 FAILS - so a new/copied wrapper cannot silently inherit the default. To change a pin or add a wrapper: edit here, run the generator.

cost_budgets.doc: Per-project monthly NOTIONAL-USD token budgets (alex-costs upgrade, 2026-07-25). Units match scripts/alex-cost-attribution.js's notional cost (a flat-Max quota-consumption proxy, NOT a cash bill; the numbers are large because they price the full token volume on a flat plan). The collector computes month-to-date cost per project and, when a project crosses warn_pct of its budget mid-month, writes a tripwire to system/cost-tripwires.json + a loud line (HQ push on the nightly path) - LEVEL-triggered, replacing the reactive 'the $40 bill crossed' discovery that forced the 07-16 cut. default_monthly_usd applies to any project without an override. Also fires a PACE tripwire when the month-to-date run rate projects to exceed 100% by month-end. CALIBRATION: values are set with ~20-40% headroom above the 2026-07 baseline (day-25 snapshot: interactive ~$27k/mo projected, prompting/email-triage ~$2k, morning-brief ~$0.6k, app-engine ~$0.6k, rest < $0.4k) so normal operation is QUIET and only a genuine spike trips it - NOT cry-wolf. Retune monthly against the real attribution table. The collector validates every override key against real project/utility/unnumbered names at read time and fails loud on a typo (a formal V14 can graduate that later without churning the V-count contract).

paths.identity_doc_note: THE IDENTITY-DOC LAYOUT (rebuilt 2026-07-25, Shaheen's call, after the byte-equality check proved to be a monitor and not a fix). History: he keeps both identity docs reachable from two folders so either location shows the current version (his words 2026-07-24: 'all display the same/most updated version'). That was done by HAND on 07-24 and had re-drifted within a day; re-unified by hand again on 07-25 and re-drifted again within 85 minutes, live, while the fix was being designed (a parallel session correctly appended a running-changes entry to the canonical and the duplicate silently fell behind). A weekly report that ends in a human re-copy cannot clear the permanence bar. THE FIX IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A CHECK: there is now exactly ONE file object per document. The real files live in `identity_doc_real_dir`; `identity_doc_views[]` are NTFS directory junctions into it, so every legacy path still resolves unchanged and byte-divergence is not detected, it is impossible. WHY A JUNCTION AND NOT A HARDLINK: measured on this machine - a replace-style save (write a temp file, rename over the target; what Word, python-docx and most editors do) SILENTLY breaks a hardlink, leaving two files that look fine to anything not checking the file id. A junction links the DIRECTORY, so NTFS resolves the path before the file is created or renamed and there is no per-file link to break; the same test through a junction kept both paths as one file. WHY THE REAL FILES SIT IN 'Story & Guides': that is the folder Shaheen actually opens (his answer, 2026-07-25), and putting the real files where the human works means the junction absorbs the extra path segment instead of him. NOTE FOR ANY FUTURE SESSION: do NOT 're-copy the canonical over the duplicate' - that step is now meaningless (a self-copy) and the instruction that used to say so has been deleted. Just edit the document once.

identity_doc_views.why: keeps every pre-existing path (manifest master_reference_md, root CLAUDE.md Change-Propagation items 7+8, and every prose pointer) resolving unchanged after the real files moved to Story & Guides

paths.identity_doc_byte_pairs_note: EMPTY BY DESIGN since 2026-07-28, and it should stay that way. This list held document copies that were genuinely separate files and so could drift; the last one (the master reference's outer copy at Alex Presentation\ALEX-OS-master.md) was DELETED on Shaheen's call 2026-07-28, closing the final drift pair. Every identity document is now exactly one file object reachable from every historical path through the junction in identity_doc_views, so byte-divergence is impossible rather than merely monitored - the same structural principle as the 2026-07-25 junction rebuild. Do NOT re-introduce a copy here to 'make a document visible in another folder': add a junction view instead. C19 still walks this list, so a future genuine pair would be caught, but an empty list is the healthy state.

meta.trifecta_doc: Trifecta classification (three-plan validation P3, 2026-07-17): the agent-security Rule-of-Two made declarative. Each project carries {private_data, untrusted_content, external_comm} booleans (the raw capability/exposure, classified honestly) + a `gate` (the mitigation). VOCAB: draft-only (Alex drafts, a human sends) | human-posts (Alex stages, a human posts) | queue-only (Alex queues an action for human approval) | read-only (never autonomously emits/writes externally) | null (no meaningful external exposure). RULE (validator V12, pure file checks): any project with ALL THREE legs true MUST carry a non-null gate from the vocab, AND that gate string MUST appear on a `## Trifecta` line in the project's work/NN/CLAUDE.md. v1 DROPS the read-only-vs-write integrations assertion (no integrations data in the manifest; deferred, see vault/research/trifecta-map.md). v1 is DECLARATIVE, not runtime-enforced.
